=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple images, particularly the top-down view, show a cluster of approximately 5-7 leaves emerging from the same terminal node)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are crowded at the apex of the stem)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3.	Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (leaves are undivided blades)
    4.	Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5.	Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6.	Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7.	Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (margins appear smooth where not damaged)
    8.	Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaves are significantly longer than wide, widest near the middle)
    9.	Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tip tapers to a distinct point)
    10.	Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (leaf narrows gradually toward the attachment point)
    11.	Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (distinct central midrib with secondary veins branching off)
    12.	Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible and prominent, arranged in a pinnate pattern
    13.	Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (leaves reflect light, indicating a smooth surface)
    14.	Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (surface appears smooth without visible hairs)
    15.	Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are distinct but do not extend far from the stem)
    16.	Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear cylindrical in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17.	Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem appears green and soft, not woody)
    18.	Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stem surface appears smooth)
    19.	Stem color: green (with some reddish/brown tinges at the nodes)
    20.	Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (stem appears uniform without ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21.	Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): unclear (close-up images show the node but stipules are not clearly distinguishable)
    22.	Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23.	Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swelling visible at the base of the leaf)
    24.	Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: Several leaves exhibit significant damage, including irregular holes and missing sections along the margins. A pink identification tag is attached to the stem. The plant is growing among leaf litter and other vegetation.
